newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian prosecutor says sex case judge should go.
newsitem.headline: Belgian prosecutor says sex case judge should go.

text.p: The judge leading enquiries into Belgium's child sex scandal should be taken off the case because he accepted a free dish of spaghetti from a group helping parents of missing children, the chief prosecutor said on Wednesday.

A defence bid to get magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte thrown off the case has stirred a storm of protest in a country where the legal system is seen as having failed abysmally for years over the gruesome child kidnapping, sex abuse and killing case.
Connerotte, who with public prosecutor Michel Bourlet leads the team that finally cracked the case two months ago, has become something of a national hero.
A ruling by the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, will not be made until Monday, but the families of some of the dead and missing children were appalled by the advice.
"There are still children missing. All this will do is prolong their suffering and, obviously, ours," Marie-Noelle Bouzet, the mother of Elisabeth Brichet who has been missing since 1989, said.
"There will be a public outcry throughout the country (if Connerotte is taken off the case)," said Paul Marchal, father of one of four girls found dead in the scandal.

Belgium's King and Queen will hold a "round table" conference on October 18 with Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck and families of victims of the scandal on the problems of missing and abused children.
"This meeting...is aimed at summing up the situation on measures taken and to be taken to fight against this terrible plague," a palace statement said.
Belgium's top prosecutor Eliane Liekendael told the court Connerotte had been compromised by the a plate of spagetti.
"I am sorry and I regret it, but the law requires his removal," she said.
"If only it was possible to find a law to avoid his removal. But I have not found one. For the first time my job weighs heavy on me," she said. The court does not have to follow her advice.

Connerotte and Bourlet are accused by lawyers for two of the 13 people charged in the affair of having shown bias by accepting a meal from the Marc et Corine group, which specialises in helping the parents of missing children.

The affair exploded on an unwitting public in mid-August with the rescue of 14-year-old Laetitia Delhez and 12-year-old Sabine Dardenne from a makeshift dungeon in a house owned by key suspect and convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.
Both had been sexually abused.
Public horror grew with the discovery over the following two weeks of the bodies of eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo and teenagers Eefje Lambrecks and An Marchal.
The body of Bernard Weinstein -- an accomplice whom Dutroux admits killing -- has also been found, and police are searching for at least seven other missing children.
"I do not understand why Connerotte has to be removed," a visibly shaken Gino Russo -- Melissa's father -- said.

There have been marches in support of Connerotte and Bourlet through the streets of Neufchateau, the centre of the investigations. A petition against their removal from the case has attracted 125,000 signatures.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who last week called for the court to be "creative" refused to comment on the matter on Wednesday.
Dutroux' lawyer Julien Pierre, who was the first to lodge the formal complaint against Connerotte, has received death threats by telephone.
Virginie Baranyanka, a lawyer representing Jean-Michel Nihoul, another key suspect in the affair, has joined Pierre in his bid to get Connerotte removed.
Whether or not the Cour de Cassation upholds the complaint against Connerotte, the early lodging of the motion for his removal opens the way for an appeal to the Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.

An appeal could add years to the case, to the annoyance of ordinary Belgians uncomfortable at the glare of adverse international publicity the case, and its revelations of police bungling -- or worse -- has shone on the country.
